title: Flow Builder fundamentals, resources, variables, and data types
objectives: Explain that a flow type in Flow Builder decides which elements and resources you can add and how you distribute the flow.
Create and use variable resources with the correct data type, including record and collection variables.
Apply official variable considerations: null versus empty string, Boolean null versus false, and input/output access.
Keep Flow resources as metadata and the records they read or write as business data.
diagnostic_question: A screen Flow on a record page must accept the current record Id, store a Boolean, and pass a collection into a subflow. Before reading, which resources and data types would you create, and what would you check if the Flow action appears to run with a blank Id?
definition: Flow Builder is where you design a flow. A flow type determines which elements and resources you can add and how you distribute the flow. Resources such as variables hold values at run time; data types (including Boolean, number, record, and collections) decide what a variable can store. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm); [Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm); [Build a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_build.htm))
why_it_matters: Wrong type, wrong data type, or a variable that is not available for input is a classic interview and debug failure: a Flow action never receives recordId, a Boolean stays null instead of false, or a subflow input name is too long. AUTO-001 chose Flow; this lesson is how Flow actually holds data.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of Flow Builder as a recording-studio mixing board. Each channel is a resource. A variable channel has a data type: text, Boolean, number, record, or a collection. Input jacks are Available for Input; output jacks are Available for Output. The board layout—the flow type—decides whether you even get a Screen fader. Blank is null unless you set EmptyString. This is not a formula field, a validation rule, or Apex syntax.
deeper_explanation: Help's Flow Types topic states that a flow or flow version's type determines which elements and resources you can add and how you can distribute the flow. A screen flow requires user interaction because it includes screens, local actions, steps, choices, or dynamic choices, and it does not support Wait elements. An autolaunched no-trigger flow runs in the background and does not support screens, local actions, choices, or choice sets. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm))

Build a Flow: after you model the process, design it in Flow Builder—choose a category and type, add elements, and connect them (auto-layout creates connectors). New automations belong in Flow Builder; Help notes Process Builder support and updates were scheduled to end 31 December 2025. ([Build a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_build.htm); [Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm))

Variable considerations: a blank field or resource is null at run time; use {!$GlobalConstant.EmptyString} to treat text as an empty string. Boolean null is not false—filters that look for false miss null. Number variables are treated as integers by default. Record and record collection variables support only Salesforce objects. Percentage values assigned onto a record variable and then used in a formula are divided by 100. ([Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm))

Available for Input/Output is a contract with callers. Disabling it can break URL parameters, subflows, and pages. Flow actions pass only the record's Id into a Text input variable named recordId; if that variable is missing, the flow still tries to run. Lightning App Builder does not support collection, record, or record collection inputs; text inputs max out at 4,000 characters. A subflow input variable API name can be up to 40 characters. Do not pass a currency merge field (it includes $) into a currency variable via URL. ([Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm))

This lesson does not replace AUTO-001 tool choice. A Flow variable is not a formula field, not a validation rule, not an approval process, and not an Apex class member. Apex-defined data types exist as a neighboring resource type—do not invent their schema here.

mental_model.analogy: A recording-studio mixing board: flow type is which board you rolled into the room; each resource is a channel with a data type; input/output are the jacks other gear can use.
useful_mapping: flow type → which board (screen vs autolaunched) and which faders exist
variable → a channel that holds a value while the interview runs
data type → what the channel will accept (text, Boolean, record, collection)
Available for Input → a jack a Lightning page, URL, or subflow can drive
recordId → the named text jack a Flow action will plug the record Id into
null vs EmptyString → silence on the channel versus an explicit empty take
collection variable → a multi-track that holds many values of one type
where_it_breaks: A mixing board does not encode Flow interview limits or DML bulkification (AUTO-006/AUTO-007).
Apex-defined types are not audio cables; look up that Help topic when they appear.
Lightning App Builder cannot drive record or collection jacks even if you wired them as input.
The analogy does not replace formula fields, validation rules, or approval routing.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Flow Builder is the design surface. The flow type decides elements, resources, and distribution. Variables hold typed values for the interview. Blank is null. A Flow action only injects the Id if you expose a Text input named recordId.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick the type first because a screen Flow can have choices and a no-trigger autolaunched Flow cannot. I create variables with a data type that matches the data: record variables only for Salesforce objects, collections for many values. I mark Available for Input only when a page, URL, or subflow must set the value. I never confuse a Flow variable with a formula field, a validation rule, an approval field update, or an Apex class property.

terminology.plain: The kind of flow, which unlocks elements, resources, and how you launch it.
terminology.precise: Help: a flow or version's type determines which elements and resources you can add and how you distribute it.

terminology.plain: A named value the flow can read or write during the interview.
terminology.precise: Variables, and other resource kinds you create in Flow Builder, hold or calculate values. Variable considerations cover null, data types, and input/output.
terminology.example: A Text variable LAB_Reason Available for Input.
terminology.non_example: An Opportunity row in the database is business data, not a Flow resource definition.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Formula field on the object: metadata outside the flow.
terminology.boundary: Constants, formulas, and choices are neighboring resources; this lesson centers variables.

terminology.plain: A resource that stores a value while the flow runs.
terminology.precise: Create a variable with a data type. Blank is null. Available for Input/Output controls callers. Record variables support only Salesforce objects.
terminology.example: Boolean variable LAB_IsVip defaulted to false, not left null.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule formula is not a Flow variable.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Assignment element: writes into a variable (AUTO-006).
terminology.boundary: Do not disable input on a variable a Lightning page still sets.

terminology.plain: The kind of value a variable is allowed to hold.
terminology.precise: Help calls out Boolean (null is not false), number-as-integer default, percentage divided by 100 in formulas from record variables, record/record collection limited to Salesforce objects, and Apex-defined as a neighboring type.
terminology.example: Record variable of type Contact versus a Text collection of email addresses.
terminology.non_example: Picklist value set on the object is not a Flow data type picker choice until you map it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex primitive types: related but not the Flow resource picker.
terminology.boundary: Currency URL merge fields include a symbol and will not bind to a currency variable.

terminology.plain: A variable that holds multiple values of one type.
terminology.precise: Used to store many records or values; Lightning App Builder cannot pass collection inputs. Subflows can receive collections if the child exposes them as input.
terminology.example: Record collection of LAB_ Tasks to create after a loop (AUTO-006).
terminology.non_example: A formula field that returns one number is not a collection.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record variable: one record, not many.

terminology.plain: The Text input name a Flow action uses to pass the current record's Id.
terminology.precise: If the flow has a Text input variable called recordId, the action passes the record Id at runtime; if not, the flow still tries to run.
terminology.example: Screen Flow on Opportunity with input Text recordId.
terminology.non_example: A formula field named recordId on the object is not this contract.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: URL parameters can also set input variables; still not validation.
terminology.boundary: Only the Id, not other fields, comes from the Flow action.

terminology.plain: Blank means null; EmptyString is an explicit empty text value.
terminology.precise: Leave a field blank and it is null at run time. To treat text as an empty string, set {!$GlobalConstant.EmptyString}. Boolean null is not false.
terminology.example: Filter Get Records where Active__c equals false, after setting the Boolean variable to false.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule using ISBLANK is a different tool.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex null: similar idea, different language.
terminology.boundary: Percentage formula scaling is a separate consideration.

when_to_use: Use Flow Builder variables when an interview must hold typed values that a formula field on the object cannot keep for the duration of the run.
Use a Text input named recordId when a Flow action should pass the current record Id into a screen or autolaunched Flow.
Use a Boolean variable explicitly set to false when a Get Records filter must match checkbox false—not null, and not a validation rule.
Use a record or collection variable when the Flow will work with Salesforce records, not when a simple formula or approval field update is enough.
Use this resource model before writing Apex parameters; invocable Apex is an action, not a substitute for Flow data types.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a Flow variable to replace a formula field that should always display on the record without an interview.
Do not use Flow resources to block illegal saves—that is a validation rule, not a Boolean variable.
Do not use a Flow variable as a substitute for an approval process when a person must approve.
Do not pass collection or record variables from Lightning App Builder; Help says those input types are unsupported there.
Do not start in Apex to hold a string when a Flow Text variable is the interview's store.

interview_questions.question: What is a Flow resource, and how is it different from a formula field?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A resource such as a variable holds a typed value during the Flow interview. A formula field computes on the record without running a Flow and is not interview storage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick the flow type first because it controls which resources exist. I create variables with data types. I do not use a Flow variable to replace a validation rule or an approval. If the value should always show on the record, that is a formula field (AUTO-001). Apex parameters are a different language.
interview_questions.example: LAB_IsPriority Boolean in a screen Flow versus a formula field on Contact that concatenates names.
follow_ups: Can App Builder pass this variable?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling every field a Flow resource

interview_questions.question: Why does a Flow action need a variable named recordId?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Flow actions pass only the record's Id, and only into a Text input variable called recordId. If it is missing, the flow still tries to run—with no Id.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I create Text recordId, Available for Input. I do not expect other fields to arrive from the action. I Get Records if I need more fields. I do not use Apex or a validation rule to inject the Id. Lightning App Builder is a different input channel with its own limits: no collections or records, 4,000-character text.
interview_questions.example: Account page Flow action launching LAB_ContactQuickCreate.
follow_ups: What if the name is RecordID with different casing?
How do URL parameters set inputs?
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming all field values are passed

interview_questions.question: Get Records using a Boolean variable returns nothing. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check whether the Boolean is null. Flow does not treat null as false. Set the variable to false, then filter.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at debug. If the resource was never assigned, it is null. I set a default or an Assignment to false. I do not fix it with a validation rule or Apex. I also remember number variables default to integers and percentage formula scaling if numbers look wrong.
interview_questions.example: Filter Active__c equals {!varBoolean} when varBoolean was never set.
follow_ups: How would EmptyString appear in a text filter?
Would a formula field on the object help?

interview_questions.question: Lightning App Builder cannot bind your collection input. What does Help say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The Flow component does not support collection, record, or record collection input variables. It only supports manually entered values, with text max 4,000 characters.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I redesign: pass a single Id as text and Get Records inside the flow, or launch a screen Flow another way. I do not switch to Apex solely for the input binding. I also do not confuse this with approval process inputs.
interview_questions.example: App Builder refusing to map a Contact collection into LAB_ScreenFlow.
follow_ups: Could a subflow pass the collection instead?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling it a platform bug without reading Help

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse to create a Flow variable at all?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a formula field, validation rule, or approval process already owns the outcome, or when Apex is only being used to hold a string the interview could store.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AUTO-001 still applies. Always-on calculate is a formula. Block save is validation. Human route is approval. Interview state is a Flow variable. I also refuse collection inputs from App Builder rather than inventing an Apex wrapper without a complementary-tool reason.
interview_questions.example: Displaying Amount times 0.1 on Opportunity is a formula field, not a Flow Number variable.
tradeoffs: Declarative record compute vs interview state
follow_ups: Can a constant replace this variable?
weak_answer_warnings: Creating variables for every object field

interview_questions.question: How do flow types change resources?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Type decides which elements and resources you can add. Screen flows can use choices; autolaunched no-trigger flows cannot have screens or choices.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I never start drawing screens on a background autolaunched flow. I pick Screen when a user must interact. I pick autolaunched when a button, another flow, or Apex should run in the background (AUTO-005). Wait is not available on screen flows per Help.
interview_questions.example: Choices on LAB_ScreenFlow versus an autolaunched child that only assigns variables.

interview_questions.question: A parent Flow fails when calling a subflow. What variable issue do you check first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The input variable API name length, max 40 characters, and whether the child still exposes that input. Disabling input on an existing variable can break the caller.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare API names and types. I do not rename casually in production. I do not replace the subflow with a validation rule. If the child is an autolaunched flow, it still cannot show screens. Apex is not the first fix for a 41-character name.

What is Available for Output for?

interview_questions.question: Teach the mixing-board analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Flow type is which board, variables are typed channels, input/output are jacks, collections are multi-tracks. It breaks on App Builder, where some jacks do not exist, and on AUTO-001 tools that are not channels at all.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add that blank is null, Boolean null is not false, and recordId is a specially named jack for Flow actions. Formula fields, validation rules, and approvals are other rooms in the building, not faders. Apex-defined types are a neighboring cable standard I will not fake.
